items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Teddy Bunn, for instance, didn't have Django's speed or technical mastery.

ctx.x: In January, Lloyd and Cecil wanted to bring Hubert Mann back into the orchestra, and we all chipped in to send Hubert his fare. The reason for bringing Hubert was that Bull Willimas had a dispute with Buchanan and took a poke at him, but missed, and some of the bouncers grabbed Bull to keep him from taking another kick at Buchanan, and he had Lloyd to fire Bull.

We took a banjo player named Teddy Bunn, until Hubert arrived from California, where it was said that he had been a member of a Holy Roly Church. Hubert arrived at the time that we were having rehearsal, with a straw hat, a light-weight suit, summer shoes, and no overcoat. Lloyd managed to get his tuxedo for the night, and when he came to work that night, he was so drunk that he went to sleep on the top of the piano, which was up, and he sat next to it, in a manner that made it easy for him to lay his head on and…

When Buchanan saw Hubert sleeping on the piano top and bouncing with the rhythm that was coming from the dancers, that made the floor bounce, which in turn made the bandstand and piano bounce, he was so angry that he could have bitten a nail in two. He told Lloyd to get rid of him right away, and there went the money we had chipped in to Hubert's train fare to New York! Teddy Bunn came back the next night and stayed with us until we finished the last of January to go on the road again.
